themes.name: riso
themes.description: Default. Riso stock printed in two inks (cobalt and vermilion, plum where they overprint) with misregistered headings, paper grain, a halftone bloom and kraft rules. The page column sits on a translucent reading panel (--tk-panel; transparent turns it off).

themes.name: riso-night
themes.description: Riso on deep navy stock with grain: cream type, sunflower links, vermilion marks and a cornflower second ink. Tape, slips, stamps and prints stay cream paper. The page column sits on a translucent navy reading panel.

themes.name: auto
themes.description: Follows the reader’s system: riso by day, riso-night in dark mode.

themes.name: paper
themes.description: Light publication: cream stock with fibre, cobalt ink, Newsreader display serif.

themes.name: graphite
themes.description: Retired brand dark (kept for existing sheets): charcoal felt with an ember glow, cream type.

themes.name: ink
themes.description: High-contrast Swiss neutral: white stock, heavy black rules, Archivo.

themes.name: slate
themes.description: Technical dark: blueprint grid, steel accent, IBM Plex Mono headings.

themes.name: none
themes.description: No kit styling; structure and behavior only.

elements.name: tk-page
elements.description: Max-width sheet column. In the riso themes it sits on a translucent reading panel over the page texture; set --tk-panel:transparent (or a colour) on body to change it.

attributes.name: wide
attributes.description: Wide 76rem column instead of the 43rem reading column; running text keeps a 46rem measure.

attributes.name: unnumbered
attributes.description: Turn off the 01, 02… numbers on section headings.

elements.name: tk-hero
elements.description: Sheet header block (h1, dek, byline).

elements.name: tk-section
elements.description: Numbered section; h2 gets a deep-link anchor when the section has an id.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: Deep-link target, also used by tk-toc.

attributes.name: unnumbered
attributes.description: No number on this section’s heading.

elements.name: tk-grid
elements.description: Responsive grid; collapses to one column under 640px.

elements.name: tk-split
elements.description: Two-column split for genuinely parallel content.

elements.name: tk-card
elements.description: Raised card on the theme surface.

elements.name: tk-callout

attributes.name: kind

elements.name: tk-stat

attributes.name: good

elements.name: tk-stats

elements.name: tk-figure

elements.name: tk-table

attributes.name: filter

attributes.name: sortable
attributes.description: Click a column header to sort.

elements.name: tk-timeline
elements.description: Vertical timeline; from JSON {items:[{when,text}]} or a plain list.

attributes.name: data

elements.name: tk-steps

elements.name: tk-kbd
elements.description: Keyboard-key chip.

elements.name: tk-code

elements.name: tk-details

sheetToParent.description: Posted on load, resize and DOM changes so the shell can size the iframe without inner scrollbars (Tacksheet shells honour up to 100,000 px).
Posted once on load by an embedded sheet: asks the shell to report its visible window (viewport) on every scroll and resize, since the sheet never scrolls itself.
Asks whether the shell accepts reader feedback right now.

sheetToParent.shape: { protocol, kind: "feedback.submit", type: "feedback.submit", token: string, payload: object, expectedRevision: number }
sheetToParent.description: Hands a reader submission to the shell. The shell shows its own Send dialog (with the terms while this reader has not accepted them) and POSTs only after the reader presses Send there; the sheet can neither accept the terms nor skip the dialog. Free text is limited to 4,000 characters and is refused whole (text_too_long, with limit), never shortened. expectedRevision is the responseRevision last heard from the shell. Token matches the async result.
Asks the shell to show a download/open button for an allowlisted same-version file.

sheetToParent.shape: { protocol, kind: "file.fetch", type: "file.fetch", token: string, name: string }
sheetToParent.description: Asks the shell for a same-review file’s bytes (sheets have connect-src ‘none’ and cannot fetch). Name is the file within the version, without any ./files/ prefix. Token matches the async result. The kit keeps two in flight and retries busy answers.

parentToSheet.shape: { protocol, kind: "feedback.status.result", type: "feedback.status.result", accepting: boolean, schemaRevision: number, responseRevision: number, mine?: boolean, accepted?: boolean, reason?: "owner_preview" }
parentToSheet.description: Shell answer to feedback.status, and pushed again after every saved reply. responseRevision counts this browser’s saved replies; accepted (read-only) says whether this reader already accepted the current terms, so a sheet can word its button; reason owner_preview marks the owner’s own preview.

parentToSheet.shape: { protocol, kind: "viewport", type: "viewport", top: number, height: number }
parentToSheet.description: Shell answer to viewport.watch, posted on every scroll, resize and frame resize and when the frame comes into view: the page’s visible window in the sheet’s own CSS pixels. top is negative while the sheet starts lower down the page. tk-scrolly uses it to keep its chart beside the step being read.

parentToSheet.shape: { protocol, kind: "feedback.submit.result", type: "feedback.submit.result", token: string, ok: boolean, responseRevision?: number, error?: string, limit?: number }
parentToSheet.description: Shell answer to feedback.submit, matched by token. error is cancelled when the reader closes the dialog, busy while another dialog is open, rate_limited after many in a minute, and text_too_long (with limit) for an over-long reply.

parentToSheet.shape: { protocol, kind: "file.fetch.result", type: "file.fetch.result", token: string, ok: boolean, name?: string, mediaType?: string, size?: number, bytes?: ArrayBuffer, error?: string }
parentToSheet.description: Shell answer to file.fetch, matched by token. Bytes travel as a transferred ArrayBuffer; the kit turns them into a blob: URL (media) or parses them (GLB). ok:false carries error instead.

materials.contrast: Tape titles: the ink must reach 4.5:1 against the tape as it lands on the page (3:1 at 24px and up, or 18.66px bold); a failing ink is replaced by cobalt, near-black or cream.
